subject: Computer Networking
title: Wi-Fi Generations Explained
description: Learn Wi-Fi Generations Explained in one minute.

hook.text: Wi-Fi 4, 5, 6, 6E, 7 — the numbers keep climbing. Each generation solves problems the last one couldn't.

buildup.text: Wi-Fi 4 brought MIMO. Wi-Fi 5 moved to 5 GHz for speed. Wi-Fi 6 added efficiency for crowded environments.

discovery.text: Wi-Fi 6 introduced OFDMA, letting the router talk to many devices simultaneously instead of one at a time.

twist.text: Wi-Fi 6E opened the 6 GHz band — a huge chunk of clean spectrum. Like adding new lanes to a jammed highway.

climax.text: Wi-Fi 7 will support 320 MHz channels and multi-link operation. Speeds could exceed 40 Gbps in theory.

punchline.text: Each Wi-Fi generation doubles down on speed, capacity, and efficiency.

quiz.question: What did Wi-Fi 6E add compared to Wi-Fi 6?
options: Access to the 6 GHz frequency band

details.summary: Wi-Fi generations from 802.11b through Wi-Fi 7 have progressively increased speed, capacity, and efficiency. Each generation introduces wider channels, better modulation, and new techniques.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding Wi-Fi generations helps choose the right equipment and explains why newer devices perform better. Each generation solved specific limitations of its predecessor.
takeaways: Wi-Fi 4 through 7 correspond to 802.11n, ac, ax, and be standards
Each generation roughly doubled or tripled maximum throughput
Wi-Fi 6 focused on efficiency in dense device environments

faq.question: What is the practical difference between Wi-Fi 5 and Wi-Fi 6?
faq.answer: Wi-Fi 6 adds OFDMA, which serves multiple devices simultaneously on subsets of a channel. Target Wake Time extends device battery life. BSS Coloring reduces interference from neighboring networks.

faq.question: Do old devices benefit from a new Wi-Fi router?
faq.answer: Old devices connect at their maximum supported standard but still benefit from a better router. Newer routers have faster processors, better antenna designs, and smarter scheduling. They handle mixed-generation clients more efficiently.
